phrases.t: I'll take a kilo of apples.
phrases.scenario: You're at the market and want to buy a kilo of apples. What do you say to the seller?
You're at the shop and want to ask for a litre of milk. What do you say?

phrases.scenario: Someone is serving you coffee with a lot of sugar, and it's too much for you. What do you say?
At the breakfast table, you want to ask for a slice of bread. What do you say?

dialogue.title: Shopping at the market
lines: How many apples would you like?
A bottle of water and a little cheese.

de-quantite.title: "Un kilo DE pommes" — the same "de" rule
de-quantite.body: After an expression of quantity (un kilo de, un litre de, beaucoup de, trop de), the article also disappears and becomes just de/d' — the same thing that happens after a negation (previous unit). Notice: you don't say "un kilo des pommes", you say un kilo de pommes.

review.why: Two PT glosses; EN equivalents depend on countable/uncountable.
EN splits by countable vs uncountable.
Fine, but the PT gloss is awkward.

review.en: That's too much sugar for me.
review.why: Natural EN may be 'That's too much sugar for me.'; literal 'It's' also fine.
'Et avec ça ?' is a shop idiom; 'Anything else?' is the natural equivalent.
